examples.ko: 저는 이 라디오 프로그램의 오랜 애청자예요.
examples.en: I'm a longtime regular listener of this radio show.
A listener's story was featured on today's broadcast.

examples.ko: 이 팟캐스트는 애청자가 점점 늘고 있어요.
examples.en: This podcast is gaining more and more regular listeners.

examples.ko: 제 친구는 그 드라마의 열혈 애청자라서 한 회도 안 놓쳐요.
examples.en: My friend is such a devoted viewer of that drama that she never misses an episode.

examples.ko: 애청자 여러분, 오늘도 방송을 들어 주셔서 감사해요.
examples.en: Dear listeners, thank you for tuning in again today.

examples.ko: 라디오 애청자라면 이 목소리를 바로 알 거예요.
examples.en: If you're a regular radio listener, you'll recognize this voice right away.

explain: '시청자'는 TV를 보는 사람, '청취자'는 라디오를 듣는 사람이고, '애청자'는 거기에 '즐겨 듣고 본다'는 마음이 더해진 말이에요. 라디오, 팟캐스트, 드라마처럼 방송에 주로 쓰고, 책이나 신문을 즐겨 읽는 사람은 '애독자'라고 해요.
explain_en: '시청자' is someone who watches TV and '청취자' is someone who listens to the radio; '애청자' adds the feeling of watching or listening because you enjoy it. It is mostly used for broadcasts such as radio, podcasts and dramas. For someone who loves reading books or newspapers, people say '애독자'.

en: worry; bother; keep someone in suspense

examples.en: I was anxious all day because I didn't hear from them.

examples.ko: 그만 애태우고 결과를 빨리 말해 주세요.
examples.en: Stop keeping me in suspense and tell me the result already.
Don't keep your parents worried for too long.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 일부러 답장을 늦게 해서 저를 애태워요.
examples.en: He replies late on purpose to keep me on edge.

examples.ko: 시험 결과를 기다리며 애태우던 시간이 길었어요.
examples.en: The time I spent anxiously waiting for my exam results was long.

examples.ko: 합격 발표를 앞두고 애태우는 친구를 위로해 줬어요.
examples.en: I comforted my friend who was fretting before the pass announcement.

explain: '걱정하다'보다 속이 타고 조마조마한 느낌이 훨씬 강해요. 내가 혼자 마음을 졸일 때도 쓰고, 위 예문처럼 남을 애태우게 할 때도 써요. 말할 때는 '애를 태우다'라고 띄어서 쓰기도 해요.
explain_en: It is much stronger than '걱정하다': it carries a feeling of being on pins and needles. You can use it when you fret alone, or, as in the examples, when you make someone else anxious. People also say it as two words, '애를 태우다'.

examples.en: My refrigerator broke down, so I requested after-sales service.
This company's after-sales service is really fast.

examples.ko: 애프터서비스 기간이 일 년이라서 무료로 고쳐 줘요.
examples.en: The after-sales service period is one year, so they repair it for free.
Where is the phone service center?
It was cheap, but the after-sales service is bad, so I regret it.

examples.ko: 애프터서비스는 어떻게 받을 수 있는지 물어봤어요.
examples.en: I asked how I could get after-sales service.

explain: 일상에서는 'A/S'라고 쓰고 '에이에스'라고 읽는 일이 많아요. 물건을 산 뒤에 고쳐 주거나 점검해 주는 것을 말하고, '서비스'만 말하면 가게에서 공짜로 더 주는 것을 뜻할 때도 있어서 달라요.
explain_en: In daily life people often write 'A/S' and read it as '에이에스'. It refers to repairs or checkups after you buy something. Just saying '서비스' can also mean a free extra given by a shop, so the two are different.

examples.en: This summer the cherries in the yard ripened to a bright red.
I bought a bag of cherries at the market.
The baby's lips are small and red like cherries.

examples.ko: 앵두 철에는 할머니 댁 마당이 붉게 물들어요.
examples.en: In cherry season, my grandmother's yard turns red.
I tried making jam with cherries and it's tangy.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 마당에서 앵두를 따 먹곤 했어요.
examples.en: As a kid, I used to pick and eat cherries in the yard.

explain: 앵두는 작고 새콤한 빨간 열매예요. 마트에서 파는 크고 달콤한 열매는 보통 '체리'라고 불러서 서로 다르게 말해요.

phrases.example: 그 배우는 앵두 같은 입술로 유명해요.
phrases.en: That actress is famous for her cherry-red lips.
phrases.nuance_ko: 작고 붉고 예쁜 입술을 칭찬하는 비유예요. 조금 옛날 느낌이 나는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A figure of speech praising small, red, pretty lips. It sounds a bit old-fashioned.

explain_en: 앵두 is a small, tart red fruit. The larger, sweeter fruit sold in supermarkets is usually called '체리', so the two names are used for different fruits.

en: be in an uproar; be in big trouble

examples.en: The child was missing, so the whole house was in an uproar.
If we keep this up and get late, we're really in trouble.
If you lost your wallet, that would be a real mess.
Even in the chaotic atmosphere, the teacher stayed calm.

examples.ko: 엄마가 알면 야단날 테니까 비밀로 해요.
examples.en: If Mom finds out, there'll be trouble, so let's keep it secret.

examples.ko: 서버가 갑자기 멈춰서 회사가 야단나는 줄 알았어요.
examples.en: The server suddenly stopped, and I thought the company would be thrown into chaos.

explain: 큰일이 생겨서 소란스럽고 난처해졌을 때 써요. '야단맞다'(꾸중을 듣다), '야단치다'(꾸짖다)와 소리가 비슷해서 헷갈리기 쉬우니 구분하세요.
explain_en: Use it when something big happens and things become noisy and troublesome. It sounds similar to '야단맞다' (get scolded) and '야단치다' (scold), so be careful not to mix them up.

examples.en: I suddenly wanted to eat ramyeon in the middle of the night.
I'm really sorry for calling so late at night.
My neighbors play loud music until late at night.

examples.ko: 야밤의 도시 풍경은 낮과 아주 달라요.
examples.en: The city scenery at midnight is very different from the daytime.
A cat visits the yard every night in the dead of night.
It's the middle of the night and the road is dark, so be careful.

explain: '한밤중'과 비슷하지만 '야밤에'는 '이런 시간에 왜?'라는 느낌이 섞일 때가 많아요. 그래서 갑자기 먹고 싶어지거나 전화가 오는 것처럼 뜻밖의 일과 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: It is similar to '한밤중' (the dead of night), but '야밤에' often carries a feeling of 'why at this hour?'. That is why it pairs well with unexpected things, like a sudden craving or a phone call.

examples.ko: 봄이 되면 산에 야생화가 활짝 피어요.
examples.en: In spring, wildflowers bloom all over the mountains.
I took a photo of the wildflowers blooming by the road.
Seoraksan is famous for its wildflower fields.

examples.ko: 이 꽃은 정원 꽃이 아니라 야생화예요.
examples.en: This isn't a garden flower; it's a wildflower.
I walked slowly through a field full of wildflowers.

examples.ko: 야생화 이름을 알려 주는 앱이 있어요.
examples.en: There's an app that tells you the names of wildflowers.

explain: 사람이 심지 않아도 산과 들에서 저절로 자라는 꽃이에요. '들꽃'과 거의 같은 뜻인데, 일상에서는 '들꽃'이 더 부드럽게 들리고 '야생화'는 안내문이나 설명에서 잘 보여요.
explain_en: These are flowers that grow by themselves in mountains and fields without being planted. It is nearly the same as '들꽃', but '들꽃' sounds softer in daily talk, while '야생화' appears more in signs and explanations.

examples.en: Palm trees stand in a row along the beach.
I rested for a while in the shade of a palm tree.

examples.ko: 야자나무 열매로 만든 주스를 마셔 봤어요.
examples.en: I tried juice made from palm tree fruit.

examples.ko: 이 호텔 정원에는 야자나무를 열 그루쯤 심었어요.
examples.en: They planted about ten palm trees in this hotel's garden.

examples.ko: 바람에 흔들리는 야자나무 사진이 제 배경 화면이에요.
examples.en: A photo of a palm tree swaying in the wind is my wallpaper.

examples.ko: 야자나무는 추운 곳에서는 잘 자라지 못해요.
examples.en: Palm trees can't grow well in cold places.

explain: '야자수'도 비슷하게 쓰는데, 휴양지 풍경을 말할 때는 둘 다 자주 나와요. 우리가 흔히 먹고 마시는 '코코넛'은 이 나무의 열매 중 하나예요.
explain_en: '야자수' is used in a similar way, and both words come up when describing resort scenery. The '코코넛' (coconut) we often eat and drink is one of the fruits of this kind of tree.

examples.en: My grandmother made yakgwa for us during the holiday.

examples.ko: 약과는 달고 쫀득해서 차와 잘 어울려요.
examples.en: Yakgwa is sweet and chewy, so it goes well with tea.
These days yakgwa is a popular snack.

examples.ko: 따뜻한 차 한 잔에 약과 한 조각이면 충분해요.
examples.en: A cup of warm tea and a piece of yakgwa is enough.

examples.ko: 약과 쿠키도 먹어 봤는데 꽤 맛있었어요.
examples.en: I tried yakgwa cookies too, and they were pretty good.

examples.ko: 선물 상자 안에 약과도 들어 있었어요.
examples.en: There was yakgwa in the gift box too.

explain: 명절이나 잔치 때 먹는 한국 전통 과자인 한과의 하나예요. 밀가루 반죽을 기름에 튀겨 꿀이나 조청에 적셔 만들어서 달고 쫀득해요. 요즘은 카페 디저트로도 인기가 많아요.

phrases.en: Compared to yesterday's overtime, today is nothing.
phrases.nuance_ko: 더 힘든 일에 비해 이 정도는 별것 아니라고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say that something is nothing compared to something much harder.
phrases.en_equiv: a piece of cake / nothing compared to that

explain_en: It is one of the traditional Korean sweets called 한과, eaten at holidays and celebrations. It is made by deep-frying wheat dough and soaking it in honey or syrup, so it is sweet and chewy. These days it is also a popular café dessert.

examples.ko: 정월 대보름에는 약밥을 먹는 집이 있어요.
examples.en: Some families eat yakbap on the first full moon of the new year.

examples.ko: 약밥에 밤과 대추가 들어 있어서 달콤해요.
examples.en: The yakbap has chestnuts and jujubes in it, so it's sweet.
Yakbap stays chewy even when cold, so it's good for a lunchbox.
I learned how to make yakbap from my grandmother.

examples.ko: 약밥이 너무 달아서 차와 같이 먹었어요.
examples.en: The yakbap was too sweet, so I ate it with tea.

examples.ko: 시장에서 약밥 한 팩을 사 왔어요.
examples.en: I bought a pack of yakbap at the market.

explain: '약식'이라고도 불러요. 보통 흰밥과 달리 달고 쫀득해서 밥보다는 간식이나 명절 음식으로 먹어요.
explain_en: It is also called '약식'. Unlike plain white rice it is sweet and chewy, so people eat it more as a snack or holiday food than as a meal.

examples.ko: 약손가락으로 눈 주위를 살살 두드려 크림을 발라요.
examples.en: I apply cream by gently tapping around my eyes with my ring finger.

examples.ko: 약손가락이 잘 안 펴져서 병원에 갔어요.
examples.en: My ring finger wouldn't straighten, so I went to the hospital.
It's hard for me to move just my ring finger on its own.
Yesterday I got my ring finger caught in a door and hurt it.

examples.ko: 약손가락에 낀 반지가 너무 꽉 껴요.
examples.en: The ring on my ring finger is too tight.
I got a small cut on the tip of my ring finger.

explain: '약지'와 같은 손가락이에요. 한자어 '약지'는 설명문이나 병원에서 자주 보이고, 말할 때는 '약손가락'이 더 편하게 들려요. 엄지, 검지, 중지, 약지, 새끼손가락 순서로 불러요.
explain_en: It is the same finger as '약지'. The Sino-Korean '약지' shows up in explanations and at the hospital, while '약손가락' sounds more natural in speech. The fingers go: 엄지, 검지, 중지, 약지, 새끼손가락.

examples.en: While walking up the mountain path, I found a mineral spring.
My family exercises at the mineral spring every morning.
The water at the spring tastes cool and clean.

examples.ko: 아버지는 매일 물통을 들고 약수터에 가세요.
examples.en: My father goes to the spring every day with a water jug.
It takes about thirty minutes to walk to the spring.

examples.ko: 주말에는 약수터 앞에 사람들이 줄을 서 있어요.
examples.en: On weekends, people line up in front of the spring.

explain: 주로 산이나 공원 근처에서 사람들이 물을 마시거나 떠 가는 곳이에요. 물 자체는 '약수'라고 하고, 장소는 '약수터'라고 해요. 어르신들이 산책과 운동을 겸해서 자주 가는 곳으로 많이 나와요.
explain_en: It is a place near mountains or parks where people drink or collect spring water. The water itself is '약수', and the place is '약수터'. It often appears as a spot older people visit for a walk and exercise.

examples.ko: 결혼식에서 신랑이 신부의 약지에 반지를 끼워 줬어요.
examples.en: At the wedding, the groom put the ring on the bride's ring finger.
I broke my right ring finger and got a cast.

examples.ko: 기타를 칠 때 약지는 힘이 잘 안 들어가요.
examples.en: When I play guitar, my ring finger doesn't get much strength.

examples.ko: 약지를 다쳐서 반지를 뺄 수가 없어요.
examples.en: I hurt my ring finger, so I can't take the ring off.

examples.ko: 왼손 약지 사이즈를 재서 반지를 맞췄어요.
examples.en: I had my left ring finger measured and ordered a ring.
Try folding your ring finger and pinky together.

explain: '약손가락'과 같은 말이에요. 한자어라서 병원, 설명문, 뉴스에서 자주 보이고, 일상 대화에서는 '약손가락'이 조금 더 부드럽게 들려요.
explain_en: It means the same as '약손가락'. As a Sino-Korean word, it appears at hospitals, in explanations and in the news, while '약손가락' sounds a bit softer in everyday conversation.

examples.ko: 다음 달에 가족들만 모여서 약혼식을 하기로 했어요.
examples.en: We decided to hold an engagement ceremony next month with just family.
Both sets of parents came to the engagement ceremony.
I had a hanbok made to wear on the engagement day.

examples.ko: 약혼식이 끝나고 다 같이 사진을 찍었어요.
examples.en: After the engagement ceremony, we all took a photo together.

examples.ko: 약혼식 없이 바로 결혼하는 커플도 있어요.
examples.en: Some couples marry right away without an engagement ceremony.

examples.ko: 약혼식에서 받은 반지를 아직도 끼고 있어요.
examples.en: I'm still wearing the ring I received at the engagement ceremony.

explain: '약혼'은 결혼을 약속하는 일이고, '약혼식'은 그것을 알리는 행사예요. 약혼식을 따로 하지 않고 양가 부모님이 처음 만나는 '상견례'만 하는 경우도 있어요.
explain_en: '약혼' is promising to marry, and '약혼식' is the event that marks it. Some couples skip a separate engagement ceremony and only hold a '상견례', the first meeting between the two families.

examples.ko: 오늘은 제가 살 테니 양껏 드세요.
examples.en: I'm paying today, so eat as much as you like.
I ate my fill at the buffet, so I'm full.
Take as much as you want, as long as you don't leave any.
There's plenty of meat, so grill as much as you want.

examples.ko: 떡볶이는 양껏 시켜도 돼요, 제가 낼게요.
examples.en: You can order as much tteokbokki as you want; I'll pay.
If you're hungry, get more and eat as much as you like.

explain: '마음껏', '실컷'과 비슷하지만 '양껏'은 먹을 수 있는 양만큼이라는 느낌이라 주로 음식에 써요. '양껏 드세요', '양껏 담다'처럼 권하거나 허락할 때 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: It is similar to '마음껏' and '실컷', but '양껏' means 'as much as you can take', so it is mostly used with food. It fits phrases like '양껏 드세요' and '양껏 담다' when offering or allowing something.

examples.en: On New Year's Day, my family had a simple meal together.
Some companies close during the New Year's holiday.

examples.ko: 우리 집은 양력설 말고 음력설을 크게 지내요.
examples.en: My family celebrates the lunar New Year big, not January 1st.

examples.ko: 양력설 아침에 해돋이를 보러 바닷가에 갔어요.
examples.en: On New Year's morning, I went to the seaside to watch the sunrise.

examples.ko: 양력설과 음력설 중 언제 떡국을 먹어요?
examples.en: On which one do you eat tteokguk, the solar or the lunar New Year?
It was New Year's Day, so the streets were quiet from the morning.

explain: 1월 1일은 보통 '신정'이라고도 불러요. '양력설'은 음력설(설날, 흔히 '구정'이라고도 해요)과 구분해서 말할 때 써요. 그냥 '설날'이라고 하면 보통 음력설을 가리켜요.
explain_en: January 1st is often also called '신정'. '양력설' is used when you want to distinguish it from the lunar New Year (설날, sometimes called '구정'). If you just say '설날', it usually means the lunar New Year.

examples.ko: 그 아이는 어릴 때 양부모를 만났어요.
examples.en: That child met his adoptive parents when he was little.
On the weekend, I greeted my adoptive parents for the first time.
The adoptive parents raised the child with great care.
She visited Korea again with her adoptive parents.

examples.ko: 양부모의 사랑 덕분에 잘 자랐다고 말했어요.
examples.en: He said he grew up well thanks to his adoptive parents' love.

examples.ko: 입양된 후 양부모 곁에서 학교에 다녔어요.
examples.en: After being adopted, she went to school living with her adoptive parents.

explain: 입양해서 키워 주는 부모를 말해요. 낳아 준 부모는 '친부모'나 '생부모'라고 하고, 높일 때는 '양부모님'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It means the parents who adopt and raise a child. Birth parents are called '친부모' or '생부모', and the polite form is '양부모님'.

examples.en: Please put a lot of lettuce in my hamburger.
Lettuce stays crisp if you wash it and drain the water.
I put lettuce and tomatoes in the salad.

examples.ko: 양상추가 너무 비싸서 오늘은 다른 채소를 샀어요.
examples.en: Lettuce was too expensive, so I bought other vegetables today.

examples.ko: 냉장고에 양상추 반 통이 남아 있어요.
examples.en: There's half a head of lettuce left in the fridge.

examples.ko: 양상추로 쌈을 싸 먹으면 고기가 덜 느끼해요.
examples.en: Wrapping meat in lettuce makes it feel less greasy.

explain: 둥글고 속이 단단한 양상추는 샌드위치, 햄버거, 샐러드에 많이 넣어요. 고기를 싸 먹는 부드러운 잎채소는 보통 '상추'라고 해서 서로 구분해요.
explain_en: Round, firm-hearted 양상추 goes into sandwiches, burgers and salads. The soft leafy kind used to wrap meat is usually called '상추', so Koreans tell the two apart.

examples.en: In science class, I learned that frogs are amphibians.

examples.ko: 양서류는 물과 땅 양쪽에서 살 수 있어요.
examples.en: Amphibians can live both in water and on land.
I heard that salamanders are also amphibians.
I observed several amphibians at this pond.

examples.ko: 환경이 변하면 양서류가 먼저 영향을 받는대요.
examples.en: They say amphibians are affected first when the environment changes.
In class, I gave a presentation on the differences between reptiles and amphibians.

explain: 개구리, 도롱뇽처럼 어릴 때는 물에서 살고 자라면 땅에서도 사는 동물의 무리를 말해요. 주로 과학 수업이나 설명에 나오고, 뱀이나 도마뱀 같은 '파충류'와 구분해서 말해요.
explain_en: It names the group of animals like frogs and salamanders that live in water when young and can live on land as adults. It mostly appears in science classes and explanations, and is contrasted with '파충류' (reptiles) such as snakes and lizards.

examples.en: I sliced the button mushrooms thinly and sautéed them in butter.
The mushroom soup is smooth and really delicious.
Please put button mushrooms on the pizza too.
I bought a pack of button mushrooms at the mart.

examples.ko: 양송이는 물에 오래 담그지 말고 살짝 씻으세요.
examples.en: Don't soak button mushrooms in water; just rinse them lightly.
I made cream pasta with button mushrooms.

explain: '양송이버섯'을 줄인 말이에요. 갓이 하얗고 동그래서 수프, 피자, 파스타에 잘 어울려요. 표고나 느타리처럼 한국 요리에 흔한 버섯과 구분해서 말해요.
explain_en: It is the short form of '양송이버섯'. Its cap is white and round, so it suits soups, pizza and pasta. People distinguish it from mushrooms common in Korean cooking, like 표고 and 느타리.

examples.ko: 양송이버섯은 볶아 먹어도 구워 먹어도 맛있어요.
examples.en: Button mushrooms taste good whether stir-fried or grilled.
I tried mushroom soup for the first time.
Please cut the button mushrooms in half.
I added button mushrooms to the stew and it tasted richer.
Stir-fry the button mushrooms and onions together in a pan.
How can you tell if button mushrooms are fresh?

explain: 말할 때는 줄여서 '양송이'라고도 해요. 장을 볼 때나 요리 이야기를 할 때 둘 다 알아듣는 말이에요.
explain_en: In speech it is often shortened to '양송이'. Both forms are understood when shopping or talking about cooking.

examples.en: He took his friend's son as his adopted son.
His adopted son visits every week to ask how he's doing.
He decided to pass the shop on to his adopted son.
The adopted son and the biological son get along very well.
I looked into the procedure for formally adopting my foster son.
At her adopted son's wedding, the mother shed tears.

explain: 입양해서 아들로 삼은 사람이에요. 직접 낳은 아들은 '친아들'이라고 하고, 같은 방식으로 딸은 '양딸'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It refers to a son taken in through adoption. A son born to you is a '친아들', and in the same way a daughter taken in is a '양딸'.

en: seafood and vegetables with mustard sauce

examples.en: We ordered yangjangpi at the Chinese restaurant.

examples.ko: 양장피는 차갑게 먹는 요리라서 더운 날에 좋아요.
examples.en: Yangjangpi is served cold, so it's good on hot days.

examples.ko: 양장피에는 해물과 채소가 가득 들어 있어요.
examples.en: Yangjangpi is full of seafood and vegetables.
The yangjangpi sauce is mustard, so it stings my nose.

examples.ko: 저는 양장피가 나오면 겨자 소스를 조금만 넣어요.
examples.en: When yangjangpi comes out, I add just a little mustard sauce.

examples.ko: 이 집 양장피가 푸짐하고 맛있어서 또 왔어요.
examples.en: This place's yangjangpi is generous and tasty, so I came again.

explain: 주로 중국집에서 먹는 한국식 중식 요리예요. 해물, 고기, 채소를 접시에 둘러 담고 겨자 소스를 뿌려 차갑게 먹어요. 겨자 때문에 먹을 때 코가 찡해져요.
explain_en: It is a Korean-style Chinese dish usually eaten at Chinese restaurants. Seafood, meat and vegetables are arranged on a plate and served cold with mustard sauce. The mustard makes your nose sting as you eat.

examples.ko: 이 회사는 양적 성장에만 집중하고 있어요.
examples.en: This company is focusing only on quantitative growth.

examples.ko: 양적 변화보다 질적 변화가 더 중요해요.
examples.en: Qualitative change matters more than quantitative change.
Judging by quantity alone, it's not lacking.

examples.ko: 두 나라의 교류는 양적 측면에서 크게 늘었어요.
examples.en: Exchanges between the two countries have grown a lot in quantity.

examples.ko: 연구에서 양적 조사와 질적 조사를 함께 했어요.
examples.en: In the study, we did both quantitative and qualitative surveys.
They pursued only quantitative expansion, and the quality dropped.

explain: 거의 '양적 성장', '양적 조사'처럼 뒤에 명사를 붙여서 써요. 반대말은 '질적'이에요. 일상 대화보다 뉴스, 발표, 보고서에서 더 자주 만나요.
explain_en: It is nearly always used before a noun, as in '양적 성장' or '양적 조사'. Its opposite is '질적'. You meet it more in news, presentations and reports than in everyday conversation.

en: subject of conversation; topic; something to talk about

examples.ko: 이번 여행은 두고두고 얘깃거리가 될 거예요.
examples.en: This trip will be something to talk about for a long time.

examples.ko: 처음 만나는 자리라 얘깃거리를 미리 생각해 갔어요.
examples.en: It was a first meeting, so I thought of topics in advance.
A celebrity wedding is good gossip material.

examples.ko: 우리는 얘깃거리도 없이 한참 앉아 있었어요.
examples.en: We sat there for a while without anything to talk about.

examples.ko: 그 영화는 사람들 사이에서 얘깃거리로 떠올랐어요.
examples.en: That movie became a talking point among people.
It's too trivial to even call a topic of conversation.

explain: '이야깃거리'를 줄인 말이에요. 사이시옷이 들어가서 '얘깃거리'로 써요. 대화가 끊겼을 때 '얘깃거리가 없다'처럼 자주 말해요.
explain_en: It is the shortened form of '이야깃거리'. It is written with a 사이시옷 (ㅅ), as '얘깃거리'. People often say '얘깃거리가 없다' when a conversation runs dry.

examples.ko: 월급날이면 어김없이 은행 앱에서 알림이 와요.
examples.en: On payday, a notification always arrives from my banking app.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 시간 약속이 어김없는 사람이에요.
examples.en: He is someone who never fails to keep a time appointment.
His calculations are always spot on.
When spring comes, the cherry blossoms bloom without fail.
It's an undeniable fact, so you can trust it.
I hate Mondays that come around without fail.

explain: 대부분 '어김없이'로 써요. '꼭', '틀림없이'와 비슷한데, '때가 되면 늘 그대로 반복된다'는 느낌이 강해요. 봄이 오는 것이나 월급날처럼 정해진 일에 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: It is mostly used as '어김없이'. It resembles '꼭' and '틀림없이', but carries a stronger sense that something repeats as expected whenever its time comes. It fits fixed events, like the arrival of spring or payday.

en: putting arms around each other's shoulders

examples.en: I took a photo with my friend with our arms around each other's shoulders.
Putting arms around shoulders comes naturally between close friends.

examples.ko: 다 함께 어깨동무 자세로 응원가를 불렀어요.
examples.en: We all sang the cheer song with our arms over each other's shoulders.

examples.ko: 어릴 때는 어깨동무가 제일 쉬운 애정 표현이었어요.
examples.en: As kids, an arm around the shoulders was the easiest way to show affection.

examples.ko: 모르는 사람이 갑자기 어깨동무를 해서 놀랐어요.
examples.en: A stranger suddenly put an arm around my shoulders, and I was startled.
The two of them left the school gate with their arms around each other.

explain: 서로의 어깨에 팔을 두르는 행동이에요. 팔을 끼는 '팔짱'과 달라요. 친한 사이에서 자연스럽고, 친하지 않은 사이에서는 어색할 수 있어요. 보통 '어깨동무를 하다'라고 말해요.
explain_en: It is the act of putting an arm around each other's shoulders, which differs from '팔짱', linking arms. It feels natural between close friends but can be awkward between people who aren't close. You normally say '어깨동무를 하다'.

en: put arms around each other's shoulders

examples.en: We walked home with our arms around each other's shoulders.

examples.ko: 아이들이 어깨동무해서 한 줄로 서 있어요.
examples.en: The kids stand in a line with their arms over each other's shoulders.

examples.ko: 친한 친구끼리 어깨동무하면 사진이 더 정다워 보여요.
examples.en: When close friends put their arms around each other, the photo looks warmer.
We sang the cheer song with our arms around each other.
After we put our arms around each other, we felt closer.
It's embarrassing to put an arm around someone you've just met.

explain: '어깨동무를 하다'를 한 단어처럼 쓴 말이에요. 서로 어깨에 팔을 두르는 것이라서, 팔을 끼는 '팔짱을 끼다'와 구분해서 써요.
explain_en: It is '어깨동무를 하다' used as a single verb. It means two people put arms around each other's shoulders, which is different from '팔짱을 끼다', linking arms.

examples.en: The room was dim, so I turned on the light.
The underground parking lot is gloomy even during the day.
I heard a cat's cry in the dark alley.

examples.ko: 비가 오는 날에는 낮에도 하늘이 어두컴컴해요.
examples.en: On rainy days, the sky is dark even in the daytime.
It's dark inside the cave, so bring a flashlight.
Let's head home before it gets dark.

explain: 그냥 '어둡다'보다 컴컴하고 조금 음침한 느낌이 있어요. '어둑하다'는 해 질 무렵처럼 약간 어두울 때 쓰고, '어두컴컴하다'는 그보다 더 깜깜하고 답답한 곳에 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: It feels murkier and slightly gloomier than plain '어둡다'. '어둑하다' is for mild darkness, like dusk, while '어두컴컴하다' fits darker, stuffier places.

examples.ko: 겨울에는 다섯 시만 되어도 밖이 어둑어둑해요.
examples.en: In winter, it's already dim outside at five o'clock.
As soon as I entered the dim forest, I suddenly got scared.
We played in the park until it got dim.

examples.ko: 저녁 무렵 집 안이 어둑해서 불을 켰어요.
examples.en: It got dim inside the house in the evening, so I turned on the lights.
It's dim outside, so be careful on your way.

examples.ko: 어둑어둑한 골목길을 혼자 걸으려니 조금 무서웠어요.
examples.en: Walking alone down the dim alley was a little scary.

explain: 완전히 깜깜하지는 않고 해 질 무렵이나 새벽처럼 조금 어두운 때에 써요. '어둑어둑하다'처럼 반복해서 말하면 서서히 어두워지는 느낌이 살아나요.
explain_en: It is used for mild darkness, like dusk or early dawn, when it isn't fully dark. Repeating it as '어둑어둑하다' brings out the feeling of slowly getting darker.

examples.en: I bought the fabric after roughly guessing the length.

examples.ko: 정확한 숫자를 몰라서 어림짐작할 수밖에 없어요.
examples.en: I don't know the exact number, so all I can do is guess.

examples.ko: 사람이 몇 명 왔는지 어림짐작해 보세요.
examples.en: Try to guess how many people came.
I guessed just from the look on their face, but I was wrong.

examples.ko: 어림짐작하지 말고 직접 재 보는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: Don't just guess; it's better to measure it yourself.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 가격을 어림짐작하는 데 익숙해요.
examples.en: He is used to estimating prices by eye.

explain: 정확히 재거나 계산하지 않고 대강 짐작할 때 써요. 근거가 부족하다는 느낌이 있어서 '어림짐작으로 말하다'처럼 약간 조심스럽거나 부정적으로 들릴 수 있어요. '대충 어림잡다'도 비슷하게 써요.
explain_en: It is used when you guess roughly without measuring or calculating exactly. It implies weak grounds, so '어림짐작으로 말하다' can sound a bit cautious or negative. '어림잡다' is used in a similar way.

examples.en: Oh my goodness, it's been a while! Who is this?
Oh my, is it already this late?
Oh my, is that story really true?

examples.ko: 어머머, 이 옷 너무 예뻐요! 어디서 샀어요?
examples.en: Oh my, this outfit is so pretty! Where did you buy it?
Oh no, I left my umbrella at home.
Oh my, has the child already grown this much?

explain: '어머'를 길게 늘인 느낌으로, 놀라거나 반가울 때 친한 사이에서 가볍게 나오는 말이에요. '어머나'도 비슷하게 쓰는데 '어머머'가 조금 더 수다스럽고 호들갑스러운 느낌이에요. 격식 있는 자리에서는 잘 쓰지 않아요.
explain_en: It is like a drawn-out '어머', a light exclamation of surprise or delight among people who are close. '어머나' is used similarly, but '어머머' feels a bit chattier and more fussy. It isn't used much in formal settings.

examples.en: A stray cat prowls the alley every evening.

examples.ko: 일요일 오후에 동네를 어슬렁거리다가 빵집에 들렀어요.
examples.en: On Sunday afternoon, I wandered around the neighborhood and stopped by a bakery.

examples.ko: 할 일이 없어서 집 앞을 어슬렁거렸어요.
examples.en: I had nothing to do, so I loitered in front of my house.
I strolled around the market with a friend, looking at things.

examples.ko: 아저씨가 가게 앞에서 어슬렁거리는 모습이 보여요.
examples.en: I can see a man hanging around in front of the shop.
Don't dawdle; get ready quickly.

explain: '산책하다'는 일부러 걷는 것이지만 '어슬렁거리다'는 목적 없이 느릿느릿 돌아다니는 모습이에요. 한가하고 할 일 없는 느낌이 있고, 수상하게 서성이는 사람에게도 써요. '어슬렁대다'도 같은 뜻으로 써요.
explain_en: '산책하다' means walking on purpose, while '어슬렁거리다' means moving around slowly with no aim. It gives a feeling of idling or having nothing to do, and it is also used for someone loitering suspiciously. '어슬렁대다' is used with the same meaning.

examples.ko: 어영부영 하다 보니 벌써 한 해가 다 갔어요.
examples.en: Before I knew it, the whole year was already gone.

examples.ko: 어영부영 시간만 보내지 말고 계획을 세워요.
examples.en: Don't just let time slip by; make a plan.

examples.ko: 시험 준비를 어영부영하다가 점수가 낮게 나왔어요.
examples.en: I prepared for the exam half-heartedly, and my score came out low.

examples.ko: 그 문제를 어영부영 넘어가면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You can't just brush that problem aside.

examples.ko: 어영부영 대답하지 말고 분명하게 말해 주세요.
examples.en: Don't answer vaguely; please say it clearly.
I drifted through the days, and the vacation was over.

explain: 뚜렷한 계획 없이 대충 시간을 보내거나, 일을 얼버무려 넘길 때 써요. 대체로 부정적이고 '어영부영 하루가 갔어요'처럼 아쉬움이 담겨요. '얼렁뚱땅'은 눈속임으로 슬쩍 넘기는 느낌이 더 강해요.
explain_en: It is used when you spend time aimlessly without a clear plan, or gloss over a matter. It is usually negative and carries regret, as in '어영부영 하루가 갔어요'. '얼렁뚱땅' has a stronger feeling of slyly getting past something by trickery.
